title.narrative: Revolutionising indicators of (un)sustainable wildlife use and trade by harnessing social media big data

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project highlights the essential role wildlife use and trade play in sustaining millions of livelihoods by providing food, income, and cultural value. Ultimately, the development of wildlife use and trade indicators seeks to inform sustainable practices and monitoring frameworks that preserve resources vital to local and Indigenous communities while protecting cultural heritage linked to traditional wildlife use. The project encourages legal wildlife markets by combating illegal trafficking, preventing economic losses, and supporting sustainable development. It also protects legitimate business opportunities in sustainable wildlife trade. Food security is enhanced by preserving wildlife resources communities rely on for subsistence. Through the uptake by governments and institutions of indicators of harvesting practices, the project seeks to ensure long-term food availability and mitigates threats caused by unsustainable exploitation of wildlife. Capacity building and knowledge transfer are key aspects, as the project provides training and workshops for policymakers and conservation practitioners through MEA platforms. It develops tools (indicators) and frameworks to help governments monitor and manage wildlife trade effectively. The project drives policy and governance improvements by helping governments make informed decisions about wildlife management. It strengthens compliance with international agreements, enhances monitoring frameworks, and promotes evidence-based conservation strategies. The socioeconomic benefits directly contribute to broader environmental goals by reducing overexploitation of species through improved monitoring and management, protecting biodiversity via sustainable use practices, and maintaining ecosystem functions. These efforts align with global conservation targets like the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), enhancing coordination between national and international conservation efforts. Key beneficiaries include local communities, particularly Indigenous peoples and traditional wildlife users, as well as government stakeholders like policymakers, conservation practitioners, and wildlife management authorities. Conservation organizations such as NGOs, research institutions, and advisory groups also benefit, alongside private sector actors involved in legal wildlife trade. The project creates a positive feedback loop where better monitoring and management of wildlife trade supports local livelihoods and global conservation goals. This synergy ensures that both socioeconomic and environmental benefits are maintained over the long term.

To create and provide standardized online monitoring frameworks and indicators for wildlife use and trade to enable near real-time tracking and analysis of wildlife trade patterns and empower policymakers and stakeholders to make informed and sustainable wildlife management decisions.
